nodes.title: Hold an anchor and a focus

anchor.snippet: type Selection = { anchor: Cell; focus: Cell };

nodes.why: A drag, a Shift-click and Shift with an arrow all keep where the selection started and move where it ends. Two cells describe every rectangle, in any direction.
nodes.alternative: Keep a set of selected cell names.
nodes.tradeoff: A set has to be rebuilt on every move and loses where the selection started, which Shift needs.

nodes.title: Derive the rectangle with min and max
nodes.why: Taking the smaller and larger row and column makes a drag from D6 to B2 the same rectangle as one from B2 to D6, and gives the summary its top-left and bottom-right corners.
nodes.alternative: Store the rectangle as it was drawn and swap the corners when the drag runs backwards.
nodes.tradeoff: Swapping on the fly has a case for each of the four directions and is easy to get wrong for one of them.

nodes.title: A ref says whether a drag is running
nodes.why: Mouse enter fires on every cell the pointer crosses; only a pressed button should extend the selection. A ref changes without a re-render and is read fresh in every handler.
nodes.tradeoff: `buttons` works for a real mouse, but a drag that leaves the sheet and comes back still needs to know it ended outside.

nodes.title: End the drag on window
nodes.why: The button can come up anywhere. Listening on `window` ends the drag even when the release happens outside the sheet.
nodes.tradeoff: A release outside every cell would leave the drag running, so the next hover would change the selection.

nodes.title: Shift keeps the anchor
nodes.why: Shift and a click extend from where the selection started, so only the focus moves. Without Shift, the press becomes the new anchor.
nodes.alternative: Extend from the last cell clicked.
nodes.tradeoff: Extending from the last click makes a second Shift-click grow the wrong rectangle, as A1 after D4 would show.

nodes.title: Move real focus with the active cell
nodes.why: The active cell has `tabindex="0"`; focusing it too keeps the keyboard, the screen reader and the next key press on the same cell.
nodes.alternative: Keep focus on the sheet and point at the active cell with `aria-activedescendant`.
nodes.tradeoff: Active descendant is valid too, but this task asks for a roving tabindex, so the checks read focus on the cell.
